nvitk.segmentation.labels¶

Label-map primitives on Image label volumes.

All functions are backend-aware (NumPy or CuPy), accept either an Image or a raw array, and return a new Image when the input was an Image (never mutate the caller’s data).

Module Contents¶

nvitk.segmentation.labels.get_label(label_img: nvitk.types.Image | Any, label_id: int, *, crop: bool = False, margin: int = 0, missing: str = 'raise') → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Extract a binary mask for label_id from label_img.

Parameters:

  • label_img – Label volume (integer-valued).

  • label_id – Label value to extract.

  • crop – If True, crop the output to the label’s tight bounding box (plus margin).

  • margin – Voxel padding around the bounding box when crop=True.

  • missing – 'raise' (default) raises ValueError if the label is absent; 'empty' returns an empty (all-zero) mask of matching shape.

Returns:

uint8 binary mask. Matches the input type (Image in, Image out).

Return type:

Image | ndarray

nvitk.segmentation.labels.combine_labels(label_img: nvitk.types.Image | Any, ids: Iterable[int], *, new_id: int = 1) → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Return a uint8 mask where any voxel ∈ ids is set to new_id, else 0.

nvitk.segmentation.labels.remove_labels(label_img: nvitk.types.Image | Any, ids: int | Iterable[int], *, fill: int = 0) → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Return a new label image where labels in ids are replaced by fill.

Unlike the BioImaging legacy implementation, this function never mutates the caller’s data.

nvitk.segmentation.labels.append_labels(mask_source: nvitk.types.Image | Any, mask_target: nvitk.types.Image | Any, *, remap_collisions: bool = True) → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Overlay mask_source’s non-zero labels onto mask_target.

When remap_collisions is True (default) any source label that already exists in the target is remapped to a new free integer (starting from max(target, source) + 1). Labels outside source keep their original IDs.

nvitk.segmentation.labels.biggest_cc(mask: nvitk.types.Image | Any, *, structure: Any = None, n: int = 1) → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

n=1 (default) keeps only the single largest component.

percentile is in [0, 1].

nvitk.segmentation.labels.apply_per_label(label_img: nvitk.types.Image | Any, op: Any, *, label_ids: Sequence[int] | None = None, dtype: Any = None, overlap: str = 'first') → nvitk.types.Image | Any¶

Run a binary operation independently on each label and recombine, preserving the ids.

Why¶

A binary operation applied to the union of several labels answers a different question from the same operation applied to each of them. Connected components over {1, 3} fused into one mask reports one component where two labels touch, and drops the smaller label entirely when they do not; a dilation grows each label into its neighbour and erases the boundary between them. Running per label and painting the ids back keeps the parcellation the caller started with, which is almost always what a multi-label selection means.

param label_img:

Integer label volume. Zero is background.

type label_img:

Image or array

param op:

op(binary) -> binary, where binary is this function’s own per-label mask, wrapped as an Image when label_img was one so the operation keeps its spacing and affine. Anything non-zero in the result is taken as foreground.

type op:

callable

param label_ids:

Labels to operate on, in the order they are applied. None uses every non-zero label. Labels not named here are copied through untouched — an operation on a selection must not delete the parts of the volume it was not asked about.

type label_ids:

sequence of int, optional

param dtype:

Output dtype. Defaults to the input’s own integer dtype, else the smallest that holds every id.

type dtype:

optional

param overlap:

Which label wins where two results cover the same voxel — the inputs are disjoint but the outputs need not be (a dilation of two adjacent labels overlaps by construction). "first" keeps the earlier label in label_ids order, "last" the later one. Made explicit because the alternative is an ordering-dependent result that looks like a bug the first time two labels touch.

type overlap:

{“first”, “last”}

returns:

Same kind as label_img, never a view of it.

rtype:

Image or array

Examples

>>> from nvitk.morphology.components import keep_largest_components
>>> cleaned = apply_per_label(
...     labels, lambda m: keep_largest_components(m, n=1), label_ids=[1, 3]
... )

Keep only slices along axis (default Z) where both masks have any label; zero out the rest in both.
